newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Conference organiser leaves Mauritius after arrest.
newsitem.headline: Conference organiser leaves Mauritius after arrest.

text.p: The organiser of a major oil and minerals conference in Mauritius who was arrested at the weekend on fraud charges flew out of the Indian Ocean island on Wednesday, immigration officials said.
They said Humphrey Harrison left for Johannesburg after paying $160,000 by cheque for conference expenses.
Lawyers said relatives earlier on Tuesday paid a Mauritian hotel up to 1.4 million rupees in bills owed by Harrison. Harrison flew out aboard a South African airways plane.

Harrison's wife Karin told Reuters in South Africa that Mauritius government officials and hotel staff refused to accept payment for outstanding conference bills through bank transfer and insisted on cash.

Her husband appeared in court on Monday on charges of conspiring to fraudently obtain credit, and the case was postponed to June 30. She said payment of around 30,000 pounds -- mainly for catering costs -- was made by bank transfer to the hotel on Monday.
On Monday, Harrison was charged and refused bail. Police said they opposed the bail application until a large proportion of money owed to the hotel arrived on Tuesday.
The conference is a showcase for sub-Saharan oil and mining with several African ministers attending. It was held for the fourth time this year.
